content.alt: Gulliver's Travels - What kind of story is it?
content.text:
What kind of story is Gulliver's Travels?

Gulliver's Travels is a story that, through a grand adventure between a land of tiny people and a land of giants, shows that "even when sizes differ, the size of the heart is the same." It's a classic adaptation of Jonathan Swift's 1726 satirical novel, retold at a child's level.

content.text:
The original story

Published in 1726 by Jonathan Swift (1667-1745) as a satirical novel for adults, it consists of four parts: the tiny land of Lilliput, the giant land of Brobdingnag, the flying island of Laputa, and the land of the intelligent horses, the Houyhnhnms. The original was social satire, but the Lilliput and Brobdingnag parts became widely established as children's tales.

content.text:
Plot summary of Gulliver's Travels

Shipwrecked at sea, Gulliver arrives in Lilliput, a land of people far smaller than himself, where he is treated as a giant. Later, in reverse, he travels to Brobdingnag, where he himself becomes tiny, and learns how to help and understand one another no matter the size.

content.text:
The moral of Gulliver's Travels

The heart of it is that even when outward appearance (size) differs, the size of the heart is the same, and we should understand and help those who are different from us. Talk with your child about facing what's different with curiosity rather than fear.

content.alt: Gulliver's Travels - How to read it aloud
content.text:
How to read it aloud

In Lilliput read small and quick, and in Brobdingnag big and slow, to make the size contrast come alive. Spark imagination with "If you became really tiny, what would you want to try?", and playing size games with finger puppets is fun too. Best suited for ages 5-7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Gulliver's Travels best for?
A. It's best for ages 5-7. The size contrast of Lilliput and Brobdingnag sparks the imagination, so children who love adventure enjoy it.

Q. Is the original a children's tale?
A. The original is a satirical novel for adults. The Lilliput and Brobdingnag parts were adapted into an adventure tale and are widely read by children.

Q. What activities pair well with it?
A. Comparing big and small objects, finger-puppet play, and drawing "what I'd want to do if I got smaller or bigger" all work nicely.
